title: Local fractions and scalar-extension telescope on every pro-etale slice
statement: Fix a prime ell, a finite normed extension E of Q_ell, its norm-integral subring A, a scheme X and a pro-etale object U. Use the continuous coefficient sheaves A_X,E_X and their inclusion [def-sfb-continuous-lattice-coefficients]. For every A_X|U-module sheaf M, extension of scalars N=E_X|U tensor_(A_X|U) M [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], restricted to A_X|U, is a colimit of M --ell--> M --ell--> ... [def-weil-pbc-integral-localization-telescope]. There is a comparison e from a colimit cocone c such that e(c_n(m))=eta(ell^(-n) tensor m), and e^(-1)(eta((a ell^(-n)) tensor m))=c_n(a m). Moreover every section x of N over an object T of the slice has a covering sieve such that along every arrow f:V->T in it there are n and m in M(V) with ell^n x|V=eta(1 tensor m). The exponent can depend on V and f.

proof.text: On a compact profinite test S every continuous function h:S->E is bounded. Since norm(ell)<1, choose n with norm(ell)^n sup norm(h)<=1. The function ell^n h is continuous into A, so h=a/ell^n. Injectivity of A->E gives equality of fractions precisely after a common later stage. This proves the regular coefficient telescope on compact tests.

Sheafification and inverse image from the point preserve the compact-test colimit. Restriction to the slice is a left adjoint and preserves it too. Tensor with M preserves colimits, and the regular tensor unitor identifies every stage with M. The tensor universal property identifies the vertex with restricted sheafified scalar extension.

On the nth stage the resulting leg sends m to eta(ell^(-n) tensor m). The integral numerator can be moved across the tensor by balancing; applying the inverse comparison gives c_n(a m). The fraction relation and sheafification uniqueness ensure restriction compatibility.

The sheafification unit of the filtered presheaf colimit is locally surjective. Each local lift is represented by an element m at some finite stage n. The telescope relation ell^n c_n(m)=c_0(m) gives the asserted local numerator equation. This does not assert a common exponent over a non-quasi-compact object.
